title: 第52章山野储粮久守之策第51章乔装胡姬绝境脱身
content_zh:
推荐各位书友阅读：藏龙覆虎魏阙寒烟第52章山野储粮，久守之策（..la）北疆秋尽，朔风卷着碎雪横掠千里荒原，枯草折腰，寒云压地。雁回关外百里山野，峰峦错落，沟壑纵横，既是阻挡北骑南下的天然屏障，也是戍边将士赖以存续的方寸疆土。大魏立国百年，北疆边患从未断绝，胡人逐水草而居，秋冬粮尽便举兵南侵，劫掠村寨、焚毁粮囤，边关守军年年疲于应战，更苦于粮草不济、补给艰难。朝廷远在千里之外，粮船辎重翻越关山耗时日久，一旦寒冬封山、暴雪断路，北疆守军便会陷入无粮可食、无援可依的绝境。乱世守边，强攻不如久守，争锋不如固本，山野储粮、就地屯守，便是北疆戍边最稳妥的长治久安之策。
此番主持北疆储粮守边大局的，是五位性情迥异、各擅所长的江湖义士与戍边骨干——沉隐忍仇、深谙人心诡道的陈近仇，骁勇善战、善布军阵的陈近啸，智计百出、通透世事的包不同，心思缜密、精于细务的花无艳，刚正果敢、稳守底线的铁寻柳。五人因缘齐聚北疆，弃江湖逍遥，守边关山河，各展所长、互补长短，于荒山野岭之间筹谋储粮大计，于乱世烽烟之中筑牢守边根基，以山野方寸之地，筑北疆万里屏障。
陈近仇为五人之中的谋主，半生沉浮江湖，见惯朝野权谋、江湖险恶，性情沉郁内敛，藏锋芒于心底，记恩怨于胸中，行事从不逞一时之快，只求长远稳妥。他深知北疆守边之难，不在于兵力寡众，不在于城池坚脆，而在于粮草根基。兵马未动，粮草先行，若无充足储粮，再精锐的将士、再坚固的关隘，终有溃败之日。过往数年，北疆守军粮草全靠朝廷调拨，官道遥远、损耗惨重，且沿途多有盗匪流寇劫掠，官吏层层克扣，真正送到边关的粮食不足三成。每逢寒冬暴雪封山，补给彻底断绝，将士饥寒交迫，百姓流离失所，胡人铁骑趁虚而入，边关屡战屡疲。
“北疆久守，必先断粮草之困。”寒岭破庙之中，残灯摇曳，陈近仇指尖摩挲着粗糙的北疆舆图，目光沉凝如寒潭，字字沉稳有力，“朝廷补给不可恃，远道运粮不可久，唯有依托山野、就地储粮、就地屯守，方能自给自足、稳守经年。胡人秋冬作乱，皆因草场枯萎、牲畜减粮，我们若能储足四季粮草，守得住寒冬，便耗得退胡骑，熬得过乱世。”
他的谋划从来不止于简单囤粮，而是一套层层嵌套、环环相扣的久守体系。首先摒弃传统平地囤粮的弊端，北疆风大严寒、雨雪频发，平地粮囤极易受潮霉变、被风雪损毁，更易被胡骑一眼窥探、纵火焚毁。陈近仇敲定核心方略，依山凿窖、借岭藏粮，利用北疆山野天然沟壑、背风岩洞，改造修筑隐秘粮窖，藏粮于山野，隐储于荒岭，既避风雪侵蚀，又避敌军窥探。其次严控粮草损耗，制定分级储粮、轮换存用之法，杜绝粮食积压霉变、虚耗浪费。最后联动军民，收拢周边流离百姓，开荒屯田、随军守边，民屯补军储，军卫护民生，形成军民相依、粮守相济的闭环格局。
陈近仇心性隐忍，思虑深远，凡事皆留后手。他知晓北疆不止有外患胡骑，更有内忧隐患，沿途官吏贪腐、军中私吞、盗匪劫掠，皆是储粮守边的大忌。为此他暗中定下规矩，所有储粮账目独立、收支透明，不经地方官吏之手，由五人共同监管、互相制衡，杜绝层层克扣、中饱私囊。同时暗中排查边关私弊，肃清军中蛀虫、地头恶匪，为储粮大计扫清内部阻碍。他素来记恩亦记仇，恩怨分明，对克扣军粮、祸乱边关者绝不姑息，对勤恳守边、一心安民者倾力庇护，正是这份沉敛刚正的性子，让将士百姓心生敬畏，无人敢轻易触碰储粮底线。
与沉敛谋断的陈近仇相辅相成的，是骁勇善战、执掌防务的陈近啸。二人同姓同心，却性情迥异，陈近仇藏于幕后谋全局，陈近啸立于阵前守四方。陈近啸性情刚烈果敢，一身戎装常年不卸，刀法凌厉、军阵娴熟，擅于练兵布防、守御疆土，是北疆储粮大计最坚实的武力屏障。他深知，再好的储粮之策，若无重兵守护，终究是为他人做嫁衣，唯有守得住粮窖、护得住屯田，方能让久守之策落地生根。
山野储粮，遍地布仓，分散隐秘的粮窖遍布百里山野，看似稳妥，却也加大了守御难度。以往集中囤粮，只需重兵守护一处，如今粮窖星罗棋布、屯田散落山野，极易被胡骑逐个偷袭、暗中损毁。陈近啸接手防务之后，立刻重整戍边布局，结合山野地形，划分守御片区，布下层层岗哨、明暗斥候，构建起全方位、无死角的山野防御网。他挑选精锐将士组建巡粮队，日夜轮值巡查山野粮窖与屯田区域，白日巡查路况、修缮防护，夜间潜伏警戒、防备偷袭，风雪无阻、昼夜不休。
北疆山野多险隘，峰高谷深、林密路幽，胡人骑兵擅长迂回偷袭、潜行劫掠。陈近啸因地制宜，依托山势险地，在各条进山要道设置拒马、陷坑、暗弩，封堵隐秘小路，只留可控通路，大幅压缩敌军偷袭空间。同时改良戍边战法，摒弃以往固守城关的呆板打法，以山野粮窖、屯田为支点，机动布防、联动支援，一处遇袭、八方驰援，让胡骑无机可乘。他治军极严，赏罚分明，巡粮将士但凡懈怠失职、擅离职守，一律严惩不贷；但凡奋勇御敌、护粮有功者，即刻论功行赏，军心士气为之大振。
秋冬时节，胡骑果然如期南下，数次潜入山野腹地，试图偷袭粮窖、焚毁屯田，皆被陈近啸提前布下的防御壁垒阻拦。最凶险一战，数千胡骑趁暴雪之夜潜行进山，避开明岗，直扑核心主粮窖，妄图一举焚毁北疆全年储粮。当夜风雪漫天，视野尽失，守军警惕性大幅下降，胡骑自以为得天时地利，悄然逼近山谷。不料陈近啸早有预判，料定暴雪之夜敌军必趁机偷袭，早已亲率精锐潜伏山谷两侧，静待敌军入瓮。
待胡骑尽数进入山谷腹地，陈近啸一声令下，伏兵尽出，箭雨破空、刀枪齐鸣。他身先士卒，提刀冲入敌阵，刀锋凛冽、所向披靡，于风雪之中纵横厮杀，硬生生将突进山谷的胡骑尽数围困斩杀。此一战，大挫胡骑锐气，缴获牛羊粮草、兵刃无数，彻底断绝了胡骑偷袭山野粮仓的念想。经此一役，北疆山野粮区彻底安稳，将士百姓皆信服陈近啸的治军守御之能，为储粮久守大计筑牢了第一道铁血屏障。
若说陈近仇定方略、陈近啸守疆土，那包不同便是盘活全局、变通施策的关键之人。包不同生性通透豁达、智计灵动，不拘古法、不泥成规，最擅因地制宜、变通施策，总能在刻板规矩、僵化制度之中找出最优解法。北疆储粮大计落地之时，诸多现实难题接踵而至，皆是包不同以玲珑智计一一化解，让整套久守之策贴合北疆实情，落地可行、长效可守。
最初推行山野屯田储粮时，最大的难题便是土地贫瘠、粮种匮乏、百姓畏难。北疆土地苦寒，砂石混杂、冻土深厚，寻常粮种难以存活，往年百姓零星耕种，收成微薄，久而久之便无人愿意费力开荒。加之连年战乱，百姓流离失所，无农具、无耕牛、无粮种，纵使划出屯田，也无人耕种。与此同时，军中将士多是习武之人，不懂农耕劳作，屯田开荒寸步难行，储粮大计一度陷入僵局。
众人皆束手无策之时，包不同细细勘察北疆水土、走访本地老农，很快摸清症结所在。北疆虽寒，却适配耐寒耐旱的粟米、黑麦、荞麦等作物，只需改良耕种时节、深耕冻土、蓄水保墒，便能大幅提升收成。他随即定下变通之法，摒弃中原春耕夏耘的古法，结合北疆气候，推行晚春解冻深耕、初夏播种、初秋抢收的适配农法，避开寒霜早冻，延长作物生长期。同时收拢周边流离百姓，以粮诱民、以地安人，凡愿意开荒屯田者，官府无偿分发粮种、农具、耕牛，耕种所得粮草，半数归百姓自留，半数纳入官储粮窖，军民各得其利、互不亏欠。
针对军中将士不懂农耕的难题，包不同推行军民互助之法，抽调擅长耕种的老农分组带队，教导将士开荒、播种、除草、收割，闲暇之时将士协助百姓修缮屋舍、防备匪患、抵御外敌，百姓助力大军屯田储粮，军民互助、同心协力。除此之外，他还盘活山野闲置资源，北疆山野盛产野菜、野果、药草、兽肉，以往无人收纳、白白浪费，包不同组织人手适时采摘、捕猎、晾晒，分类储存，补充主粮不足，极大丰富了储粮品类，缓解了主粮储备压力。
包不同最过人之处，便是懂得取舍变通、平衡利弊。储粮初期，有人提议严苛管控、尽数收缴，杜绝私藏，以求官储充盈。包不同断然否决，直言“民无余粮则心不安，民不安则守不固”。乱世守边，民心为本，若一味严苛搜刮，百姓无以为生，必然流离逃亡，北疆只剩孤军，终究难以久守。唯有让利惠民、藏富于民，让百姓安居乐业、衣食无忧，方能凝聚民心，军民同心共守北疆。这番通透见解，让陈近仇深以为然，最终定下“官储固本、民储辅之、军民共守”的核心准则，让储粮久守之策兼具刚性底线与柔性温度。
大计定局、防务成型、章法落地，而细碎繁杂的实操管控、粮草养护、账目明细、民生安抚等琐事，皆由心思细腻、处事周全的花无艳全权执掌。花无艳性情温润、心思缜密，观事入微、行事稳妥，最擅打理细务、统筹琐碎、查漏补缺，于无声处完善全局漏洞，让整套储粮体系有条不紊、精密运转。世人多以貌取人，误以为她性情柔和便无杀伐决断，却不知她温柔藏锋芒、细致有乾坤，看似柔弱，却能稳住最繁杂的后勤根基。
山野粮窖修筑、粮草收纳、分类储存、防潮防虫、轮换更替，每一处细节皆关乎储粮成败。花无艳亲自带队勘察每一处粮窖选址，核查岩壁坚固度、通风干湿程度、隐蔽安全性能，不合格者一律返工重建，绝不敷衍将就。北疆昼夜温差极大，白日暖阳干燥，夜间寒霜凝露，粮窖极易返潮霉变、滋生虫鼠。花无艳潜心钻研储粮养护之法，结合北疆气候，摸索出一套专属的存粮流程：粮窖底部铺干草、铺木炭吸湿防潮，中层分区存放不同品类粮草，顶层预留通风缝隙，定期开窗通风、翻晒粮草，杜绝霉变损耗。
她将所有粮窖统一编号、分区管理，每一处粮窖单独登记台账，详细记录入粮时间、粮食品类、储存数量、轮换日期，做到账物相符、有据可查。为避免粮草积压过期、新旧混杂，她制定严格的轮换机制，遵循“先储先用、新储后用”的原则，定期取出旧粮拨付军民食用，补入新粮循环更替，确保所有储粮常年新鲜、无腐无耗。相较于军中粗放的管理模式，花无艳的管控细致入微、严苛规范，哪怕一石一粟的损耗，都会细细核查缘由、整改漏洞，数月下来，北疆山野储粮损耗率不足一成，远低于以往朝廷调拨粮草的五成损耗。
除了粮草管护，花无艳更擅长安抚民心、调和矛盾。屯田百姓与戍边将士偶有摩擦纠纷，粮草分配、土地划分、劳作分工常有争议，旁人要么严苛镇压、要么置之不理，唯有花无艳耐心倾听各方诉求，公允决断、情理兼顾，既守规矩底线，又顾人情冷暖。百姓感念她的温柔体恤，将士敬服她的处事公允，边疆民心安稳、军心和睦，无人滋事作乱，为储粮久守大计营造了安稳平和的内部环境。她从不争功、从不张扬，默默坐镇后方，打理万千细务，让前方将士无忧征战，让全局谋划落地生根，是整套久守之策最稳固的后勤基石。

最后坐镇全局、坚守底线、肃正风气、执掌裁决的，是刚正不阿、铁面无私的铁寻柳。铁寻柳一身硬功、一身风骨，行事坦荡正直、不偏不倚、不畏强权、不徇私情，守得住规矩、扛得住压力、辨得清善恶，是五人团队中的底线与标尺，更是北疆储粮守边大局的正义屏障。储粮事关军民生计、边关安危，利益纠葛极深，难免有人心生贪念、妄图钻营牟利，若无铁规约束、铁血裁决，再好的谋划、再完善的体系，终将毁于贪腐私欲。
铁寻柳专职执掌军纪规矩、粮草监察、奖惩裁决，凡涉及储粮贪腐、私吞粮草、失职渎职、扰民乱边者，无论身份高低、功劳大小、亲疏远近，一律秉公处置、绝不姑息。北疆旧部有校尉自持戍边有功，暗中私藏粮草、克扣百姓屯田收成，暗中倒卖军储牟利，事发之后，众人因其劳苦功高，纷纷求情，希望从轻处置。铁寻柳不为所动，直言“边规无私情，粮草无特例，今日纵有功之贪，明日便有无功之盗，千里之堤溃于蚁穴，储粮大局绝不容半点私弊”，最终依律严惩，革除官职、追缴赃粮、公示全军全境，震慑所有心怀不轨之人。
不止肃正贪腐，铁寻柳更着力肃清边关乱象。北疆山野盗匪横行，常年劫掠屯田百姓、偷袭运粮队伍、损毁山野粮囤，过往官府无力清剿、守军无暇顾及，盗匪愈发猖獗。铁寻柳性情刚猛、战力强悍，亲自带队清剿山野盗匪，除恶务尽、绝不留情。他不恃蛮力、善用谋略，先探查盗匪巢穴、摸清出没规律，再分兵合围、精准清剿，短短月余，北疆百里山野盗匪尽数肃清，运粮通路畅通无阻，屯田区域安稳无扰。
他守规矩却不迂腐，严律法却懂体恤。对于无心失职、知错能改者，从轻惩戒、以儆效尤；对于勤恳履职、一心为公者，倾力嘉奖、大力扶持；对于流离失所、困苦无依的百姓，多方帮扶、体恤安抚。刚正铁血与仁厚体恤兼具，让北疆全境风气清正、秩序井然，无人敢犯储粮禁令、无人敢乱边关法度，为山野储粮、长久守边筑牢了规矩底线。
五人各司其职、各展所长，彼此同心、互为臂膀，于北疆荒岭之间步步为营、层层深耕，将山野储粮、久守安边的宏图大略，一点点落地为实实在在的边关根基。陈近仇运筹帷幄、定全局方略，隐忍布局、深谋远虑，筑牢久守之根；陈近啸铁血戍边、掌山野防务，厉兵秣马、御敌门外，筑牢久守之盾；包不同灵动变通、解实操难题，因地制宜、盘活全局，畅通久守之路；花无艳细致入微、理后勤细务，精管细护、安稳民心，夯实久守之基；铁寻柳铁面无私、肃边关风气，严明法度、肃清弊乱，守住久守之底。
历经半载深耕，北疆山野面貌焕然一新。曾经荒芜贫瘠、荒无人烟的山野沟壑，如今层层梯田错落排布，片片良田沃野孕育生机；曾经隐秘破败的天然岩洞，尽数改造为规整坚固的生态粮窖，依山而藏、隐秘安稳、储粮充盈；曾经流离失所、饥寒交迫的边关百姓，如今安居屯田、劳作有度、衣食无忧；曾经军心涣散、疲于应战的戍边将士，如今粮草充足、士气高昂、守御有力。百里山野，粮草丰盈、兵民安稳、壁垒坚固，彻底摆脱了依赖朝廷远道补给的被动局面，实现了自给自足、四季无忧的储粮格局。
秋冬寒至，暴雪封山，千里雪原隔绝内外，朝廷官道彻底断绝，北疆彻底陷入孤立无援的绝境。往年此刻，边关必是粮草告急、人心惶惶、烽烟四起，胡骑肆意劫掠、边关节节败退。而今年寒冬，北疆全境安稳太平，山野粮窖储粮充足，军民衣食无忧、心气安稳。胡骑数次集结南下，眼见北疆壁垒森严、粮草充盈、军民同心，无机可乘、无利可图，几番试探之后便悻悻退去，不敢再轻易进犯。
寒夜漫漫，雪落千山，五人立于雁回关城楼之上，俯瞰苍茫雪原、遥望万家灯火。朔风凛冽，吹起衣角猎猎作响，眼底山河安稳、境内民生安定，皆是众人半载苦心耕耘的成果。陈近仇目光悠远，沉声说道：“乱世守边，不在于一时决胜，而在于长久固本。粮草为兵民之命、边关之根，藏粮于山野，蓄力于方寸，方能守得住北疆、护得住苍生、稳得住乱世。”
陈近啸颔首握拳，目光坚毅：“只要粮草不竭、军心不散、民心不乱，北疆山河，便无人可破。”
包不同笑意通透，淡然开口：“无一成不变之规，无固守不变之法，因地制宜、顺势而为，方能让久守之策生生不息、岁岁安稳。”
花无艳望着山下安稳村落，语气温和却坚定：“细处守稳、实处筑牢，日积月累、久久为功，便是边关最长治久安的大道。”
铁寻柳身姿挺拔、正气凛然：“规矩不废、本心不改，守粮守民、守土守心，北疆永固，乱世可安。”
北疆山野储粮，从来不是一时权宜之计，而是千秋久守之策。五人同心共济、各尽所能，以谋定局、以武守土、以智施策、以细固本、以正立规，于荒寒绝境之中寻生机，于乱世烽烟之中筑安宁。藏粮于山野，蓄力于边疆，安民心、固军心、御外患、肃内弊，让千里北疆再无粮草之困、再无饥寒之苦、再无失守之忧。
岁月轮转、寒来暑往，北疆山野岁岁丰收、年年储粮，壁垒日固、民心日聚、军心日盛。昔日战乱频仍、民生凋敝的苦寒边疆，终成兵民安居、粮草充盈、山河稳固的塞上雄关。乱世浮沉，山河动荡，唯有固本培元、久久为功，方能抵御万变风波。山野储粮，储的不止是四时粮草，更是边关万里安宁、苍生万世安稳、山河千秋永固。五人以侠心守家国，以智谋定边陲，以坚守赴山河，于北疆荒原之上，书写了一段乱世久守、固本安邦的千秋篇章。..la

Recommended reading for all book friends: Hidden Dragon Covers Tiger, Wei Que Hanyan, Chapter 52: Storing Grain in the Mountains, a Strategy for Long-term Defense (..la) Autumn is coming to an end in Northern Xinjiang, and the new wind sweeps across thousands of miles of wasteland with scattered snow, withered grass bending down, and cold clouds pressing down on the ground. The hundreds of miles of mountains and plains outside Yanhui Pass, with scattered peaks and crisscrossing ravines, are not only a natural barrier to prevent the Northern Cavalry from moving south, but also a small territory that the border guards rely on for their survival. The Wei Dynasty was founded a hundred years ago, and the border troubles in the northern frontier have never been eliminated. The Hu people lived in pursuit of water and grass. In autumn and winter, when food was exhausted, they sent troops to invade south, plundered villages and burned grain stores. The border defenders were tired of fighting every year, and they also suffered from insufficient food and supplies. The imperial court was thousands of miles away, and it took a long time for the grain ships to cross the mountains. Once the mountains were closed in the cold winter and the roads were cut off by heavy snowfalls, the defenders in northern Xinjiang would be in a desperate situation with no food to eat and no help to rely on. In troubled times, it is better to defend the border for a long time than to attack by force, and to consolidate the base to fight for the front. Storing grain in the mountains and garrisoning on the spot is the most reliable strategy for long-term peace and stability in northern Xinjiang.
In charge of the overall situation of grain storage and border defense in Northern Xinjiang this time are five heroes and border guards with different personalities and specialties - Chen Jinchou, who tolerates hatred and understands the deceit of people's hearts; Chen Jinxiao, who is brave and good at fighting and good at setting up military formations; Bao BuTong, who is resourceful and well-versed in world affairs; Hua Wuyan, who is thoughtful and good at details; Tie Xunliu, who is upright and courageous and sticks to the bottom line. The five people gathered in the northern frontier due to fate, abandoning their leisurely life and guarding the border mountains and rivers. They each showed their strengths and complemented each other's strengths. They planned a grain storage plan in the barren mountains and wild ridges, built a solid foundation for guarding the border amidst the wars of troubled times, and used the mountains and wilderness to build a barrier thousands of miles away in the northern frontier.
Chen Jinchou is the mastermind among the five. He has been up and down for most of his life. He is accustomed to the machinations of the government and the opposition, and the dangers of the world. He has a gloomy and introverted temperament. He hides his edge in his heart and keeps grudges in his heart. He never acts quickly, but only seeks long-term stability. He knew that the difficulty in guarding the northern frontier lay not in the small number of troops or the fragility of the city, but in the foundation of food and grass. Before the soldiers and horses move, food and grass go first. If there is no sufficient food storage, no matter how elite the soldiers are or how strong the passes are, they will eventually be defeated. In the past few years, the northern Xinjiang defenders relied entirely on the imperial court to allocate food and grass. The official roads were far away and suffered heavy losses. There were many bandits and bandits plundering along the way. Officials withheld at all levels, and less than 30% of the food was actually delivered to the border. During the cold winter, snowstorms closed the mountains, and supplies were completely cut off. The soldiers were hungry and cold, and the people were displaced. The barbarian cavalry took advantage of the situation, and the border guards were exhausted from repeated battles.
"If you defend the Northern Territory for a long time, you must first cut off the shortage of food and grass." In the ruined temple in Hanling, the remaining lamps were swaying. Chen Jinchou rubbed the rough map of Northern Territory with his fingertips. His eyes were as cold as a cold pool, and the words were steady and powerful. "The imperial court cannot rely on supplies, and transporting food from long distances cannot last long. Only Relying on the mountains and fields, storing grain on site, and staying on site, we can be self-sufficient and maintain stability throughout the years. The Hu people are in trouble in autumn and winter because the pastures wither and the livestock reduces grain. If we can store enough grain for the four seasons and survive the cold winter, we will be able to use up the Hu cavalry and survive the troubled times."
His plan has never been limited to simply stocking up on food, but a long-term defense system that is nested and interlocked. First of all, abandon the disadvantages of traditional grain storage on flat ground. Northern Xinjiang is windy and cold, with frequent rain and snow. Grain storage on flat ground is extremely susceptible to moisture, mildew, damage by wind and snow, and is even more susceptible to being spied on by horsemen and set on fire. Chen Jinqiu finalized the core strategy, digging cellars in the mountains and borrowing ridges to store grain. He used the natural ravines and leeward caves in the mountains of northern Xinjiang to renovate and build secret grain cellars. He hid grain in the mountains and hidden in the wild ridges to avoid wind and snow erosion and the prying eyes of the enemy. Secondly, strictly control the loss of grain and grass, and formulate methods for grading grain storage and rotation to prevent grain backlog, mildew, wastage and waste. Finally, the army and the people were mobilized to gather the surrounding displaced people, open up wasteland and farm fields, and guard the borders with the army. The people gathered in the villages to replenish the military reserves, and the army protected the people's livelihood, forming a closed-loop pattern in which the army and the people depended on each other and food and security were supported.
Chen Jinqiu has a tolerant nature, has far-reaching thoughts, and always leaves everything behind. He knew that northern Xinjiang was not only plagued by foreign invaders, but also internal dangers. Corruption of officials, embezzlement by the military, and plunder by bandits along the way were all major taboos for storing grain and guarding the border. For this reason he secretlySet a rule that all grain storage accounts should be independent and revenue and expenditure transparent. They should not go through the hands of local officials. They should be jointly supervised by five people and check and balance each other to prevent embezzlement and personal enrichment at all levels. At the same time, they secretly investigated private corruption at the border, eliminated worms and local bandits in the army, and cleared internal obstacles for the grain storage plan. He always remembers gratitude and grudges, and has clear grudges. He will never tolerate those who deduct military rations and cause trouble at the border. He will protect those who diligently guard the border and are dedicated to peace of the people. It is this calm and upright temperament that makes the soldiers and the people feel in awe, and no one dares to touch the bottom line of the grain reserves easily.
Complementing Chen Jinqiu, who is making plans with Shen Lian, is Chen Jinxiao, who is brave and good at fighting and is in charge of defense. The two have the same surname but different personalities. Chen Jinchou hides behind the scenes and plots the overall situation, while Chen Jinxiao stands in front of the formation and guards all sides. Chen Jinxiao has a strong and courageous temperament. He never takes off his military uniform all year round. He has sharp sword skills and skilled military formations. He is good at training troops to deploy defenses and defend territory. He is the most solid force barrier for the grain storage plan in Northern Xinjiang. He knew very well that no matter how good the grain storage strategy was, if it was not protected by heavy troops, it would end up being a wedding dress for others. Only by guarding the grain cellar and protecting the farmland could the strategy of long-term storage take root.
Grain is stored in the mountains and wilds, with warehouses scattered all over the place, and secret grain cellars scattered throughout hundreds of miles of mountains and fields. It seems safe, but it also makes it more difficult to defend. In the past, when grain storage was centralized, only one place had to be guarded by heavy troops. Nowadays, grain cellars are scattered all over the place and fields are scattered in the mountains. It is extremely easy for barbarian cavalry to sneak attack one by one and destroy them secretly. After Chen Jinxiao took over the defense, he immediately reorganized the border defense layout, divided the defense areas into combination with the mountain terrain, and deployed layers of sentries and light and dark scouts to build an all-round mountain defense network with no blind spots. He selected elite soldiers to form a grain patrol team, which took turns to patrol the mountain grain cellars and farm areas day and night. They patrolled the roads and repaired and protected them during the day, and lurked at night to guard against sneak attacks, all day and night, regardless of wind or snow.
Northern Xinjiang has many dangerous mountains and passes, high peaks and deep valleys, dense forests and secluded roads. The Hu cavalry is good at making roundabout attacks and stealth plundering. Chen Jinxiao adapted measures to local conditions and relied on the dangerous mountainous terrain to set up horse traps, traps, and concealed crossbows on each of the main routes into the mountains, blocking hidden paths and leaving only controllable access roads, greatly reducing the enemy's sneak attack space. At the same time, we improved our border defense tactics, abandoning the rigid approach of defending city gates in the past. We used mountain grain cellars and farms as fulcrums to deploy mobile defenses and provide coordinated support. When one place was attacked, reinforcements came from all directions, leaving no opportunity for Hu Qi to take advantage of. He governed the army very strictly, with clear rewards and punishments. Any officers and soldiers patrolling the food supply who neglected their duties or left their posts without authorization would be severely punished. Anyone who bravely defended the enemy and protected the food supplies would be immediately rewarded according to their merits, which greatly boosted the morale of the army.
In the autumn and winter, Hu Qi went south as expected, sneaking into the hinterland of the mountains several times, trying to raid grain cellars and burn down farmland, but was blocked by the defensive barriers set up by Chen Jinxiao in advance. In the most dangerous battle, thousands of Huqi took advantage of the blizzard night to sneak into the mountains, avoiding the bright hills, and went straight to the core main grain storehouse, trying to burn down the entire year's grain storage in Northern Xinjiang in one fell swoop. That night, when the sky was full of wind and snow, all vision was lost, and the vigilance of the defenders dropped significantly. Hu Qi thought he had the right time and place, and quietly approached the valley. Unexpectedly, Chen Jinxiao had already predicted that the enemy would take the opportunity to attack during the blizzard night. He had already led his elite troops to lurk on both sides of the valley, waiting for the enemy to attack.
When all the Hu cavalry entered the hinterland of the valley, Chen Jinxiao gave an order and all the ambush troops came out. Arrows rained through the sky and swords and guns were fired. He took the lead and rushed into the enemy's formation with his sword. The blade was sharp and invincible. He fought in the wind and snow, and forcibly surrounded and killed all the Hu cavalry who rushed into the valley. This battle greatly dampened the spirit of Hu Qi, and captured cattle, sheep, food, and countless weapons, completely eliminating Hu Qi's idea of ​​sneak attacks on mountain granaries. After this battle, the mountainous grain areas in northern Xinjiang were completely stabilized. The soldiers and civilians all believed in Chen Jinxiao's ability to manage the army and defend the army, which built the first iron-blooded barrier for the long-term plan to store grain.
If Chen Jinqiu determines the strategy and Chen Jinxiao defends the territory, then Bao Bubu is the key person to revitalize the overall situation and adapt strategies. Bao BuTong has a transparent and open-minded nature, and is smart and clever. He does not stick to ancient methods and is not clumsy.He is good at adapting to local conditions and implementing flexible policies, and he can always find the optimal solution among rigid rules and rigid systems. When the grain storage plan in Northern Xinjiang was implemented, many practical problems came one after another. Bao BuTong solved them one by one with exquisite wisdom, making the entire long-term strategy consistent with the actual situation in Northern Xinjiang, feasible in implementation, and sustainable in the long term.
When the grain storage in the mountains and fields was first implemented, the biggest problem was the barren land, lack of grain seeds, and people's fear of hardship. The land in northern Xinjiang is bitterly cold, mixed with sand and gravel, and the frozen soil is deep, making it difficult for ordinary grains to survive. In the past, people cultivated sporadically, and the harvest was meager. As time went by, no one was willing to work hard to open up wasteland. In addition, due to years of war, the people were displaced, without farm tools, cattle, or grain seeds. Even if the fields were set aside for farming, no one would cultivate them. At the same time, most of the lieutenants in the army were martial arts practitioners and did not understand farming. It was difficult to open up wasteland for farming, and the grain storage plan was at a deadlock.
When everyone was at a loss, Bao BuTong carefully surveyed the water and soil in northern Xinjiang, visited local old farmers, and quickly figured out the crux of the problem. Although northern Xinjiang is cold, crops such as corn, rye, and buckwheat are suitable for cold and drought resistance. As long as the farming season is improved, the frozen soil is deeply plowed, and water and moisture are stored, the harvest can be greatly increased. He immediately decided on a flexible method, abandoning the ancient method of spring plowing in the Central Plains and working in the summer. Combined with the climate of northern Xinjiang, he implemented an adapted agricultural method of deep plowing in late spring, sowing in early summer, and harvesting in early autumn to avoid frost and early freezing and extend the growing period of crops. At the same time, we gathered the displaced people in the surrounding areas, lured them with grain, and settled them with land. To those who were willing to open up wasteland for farming, the government distributed grain seeds, farm tools, and cattle for free. Half of the grain and grass obtained from farming was retained by the people, and the other half was included in the official grain storage. Each army and the people benefited from each other and did not owe each other.
In order to solve the problem of military officers who did not understand farming, Bao Bubu promoted the method of military-civilian mutual assistance. He assigned veteran farmers who were good at farming to lead teams and taught the officers to clear land, sow, weed, and harvest. In their spare time, the officers helped the people repair their houses, guard against bandits, and resist foreign enemies. The people helped the army to farm and store grain. The army and the people worked together to help each other. In addition, he also revitalized idle resources in the mountains and fields. The mountains and fields in northern Xinjiang are rich in wild vegetables, wild fruits, medicinal herbs, and animal meat. In the past, no one collected them and they were wasted. He arranged for different organizations to pick, hunt, dry, and store them in categories to supplement the shortage of staple grains. This greatly enriched the categories of stored grains and alleviated the pressure on staple grain reserves.
The most outstanding thing about Bao BuTong is that he knows how to make trade-offs and balance the pros and cons. In the early days of grain storage, some people proposed strict control, collection of all grains, and elimination of private storage in order to fill the official reserve. Bao Tongtong categorically rejected it, saying bluntly, "If the people don't have enough food, they will be uneasy, and if the people are uneasy, they will not be able to stand firm." In troubled times, the people's heart is the most important thing to defend the border. If the raids are carried out strictly, the people will have no way to make a living and will inevitably flee. There will be only a lone army left in the northern border, and it will be difficult to defend it for a long time. Only by benefiting the people, hiding wealth among the people, and allowing the people to live and work in peace and contentment, and have food and clothing without worries, can the people's hearts be united and the army and the people work together to defend the northern border. Chen Jinqiu was deeply convinced by this insightful insight, and finally established the core principle of "consolidating the foundation with official reserves, supplementing them with civilian reserves, and cooperating with the military and civilians", so that the strategy of long-term grain storage has both a rigid bottom line and a flexible temperature.
The grand plan is finalized, defense is formed, and regulations are implemented, but the detailed and complicated practical management and control, food and grass maintenance, account details, people's livelihood comfort and other trivial matters are all handled by Hua Wuyan, who is meticulous and considerate. Hua Wuyan has a gentle temperament, thoughtful thinking, careful observation, and prudent behavior. She is best at taking care of details, coordinating trivial matters, checking for leaks and filling gaps, and improving the overall loopholes in the silent place, so that the entire grain storage system operates in an orderly and precise manner. Most people in the world judge people by their appearance, mistakenly thinking that her gentle temperament means she is not decisive in killing, but they don't know that her gentleness hides her sharpness and her meticulousness. She may seem weak, but she can stabilize the most complicated logistical foundation.
Every detail of mountain grain cellar construction, grain storage, classified storage, moisture and insect protection, and rotation is related to the success or failure of grain storage. Hua Wuyan personally led a team to survey the location of each grain cellar, checking the solidity of the rock walls, ventilation, dryness and humidity levels.Degree, hidden safety performance, those who fail will be reworked and rebuilt, and will never be perfunctory. The temperature difference between day and night in northern Xinjiang is huge. The sun is warm and dry during the day, and the frost is condensing at night. Grain cellars are prone to moisture, mildew, and the breeding of insects and rats. Hua Wuyan devoted himself to studying the methods of grain storage and maintenance, and combined with the climate in northern Xinjiang, he developed an exclusive grain storage process: hay and charcoal are laid at the bottom of the grain cellar to absorb moisture and prevent moisture. Different types of grains are stored in the middle layer. Ventilation gaps are reserved on the top floor. Windows are regularly opened for ventilation and grain drying to prevent mildew and loss.
She uniformly numbers and manages all grain cellars in separate areas. Each grain cellar is registered separately and records in detail the time of grain input, grain category, storage quantity, and rotation date, so that the accounts are consistent and well-documented. In order to avoid the backlog of expired grain and grass and the mixing of old and new grains, she formulated a strict rotation mechanism and followed the principle of "store first, use first, store new and use later". She regularly took out old grains for military and civilian consumption, and replenished them with new grains for circulation, ensuring that all stored grains are fresh all year round, free from decay and consumption. Compared with the extensive management model in the military, Hua Wuyan's management is meticulous and strict. Even if a stone or a drop is wasted, the cause will be carefully checked and the loopholes will be rectified. Over the past few months, the loss rate of grain storage in the mountains and fields of northern Xinjiang is less than 10%, which is far lower than the 50% loss of grain allocated by the court in the past.
In addition to managing food and grass, Hua Wuyan is better at appeasing people and mediating conflicts. There were occasional frictions and disputes between the people in the fields and the border guards. There were often disputes over the distribution of grain and grass, the division of land, and the division of labor. Others either severely suppressed it or ignored it. Only Hua Wuyan patiently listened to the appeals of all parties, made fair decisions, took into account both reason and reason, and not only abided by the bottom line of the rules, but also took into account the warmth and warmth of human beings. The people were grateful for her gentleness and consideration, and the soldiers respected her fairness in handling matters. The people in the border areas were stable and the military was harmonious, and no one caused trouble or chaos, creating a stable and peaceful internal environment for long-term storage of grain. She never strives for credit or shows off, but quietly sits at the rear and takes care of countless details, allowing the soldiers at the front to fight without worries and allowing the overall plan to take root. She is the most stable logistical cornerstone of the entire long-term strategy.
In the end, the one who takes charge of the overall situation, sticks to the bottom line, corrects the atmosphere, and makes the decision is the upright and selfless Tie Xunliu. Tie Xunliu is a man of hard skills and character. He is upright, impartial, unafraid of power, and not partial to selfish interests. He can abide by rules, withstand pressure, and distinguish between good and evil. He is the bottom line and yardstick of the five-person team, and he is also the righteous barrier for the overall situation of grain storage and border defense in Northern Xinjiang. Grain storage is related to the livelihood of soldiers and civilians, as well as border security. Interests are deeply entangled. It is inevitable that some people will be greedy and try to make profits. Without iron rules and iron-blooded decisions, no matter how well planned or perfect the system is, it will eventually be destroyed by corruption and selfish desires.
Tie Xunliu is in charge of military discipline and rules, grain supervision, rewards and punishments. Anyone involved in grain storage, corruption, misappropriation of grain, dereliction of duty, and disturbing the public will be dealt with impartially and will not be tolerated, regardless of status, credit, or distance. There was a lieutenant in the old northern Xinjiang army who had made great achievements in guarding the border. He secretly hid grain and grass, deducted the harvest from the people's fields, and secretly resold military reserves for profit. After the incident, everyone begged for mercy because of their hard work and merit, hoping to be dealt with leniently. Tie Xunliu was unmoved and said bluntly, "There are no selfish feelings in border regulations, and there are no exceptions in grain and grass. Even if there is meritorious greed today, tomorrow there will be unmerited thefts. Thousands of miles of embankments collapsed in ant nests. The overall situation of grain storage must not tolerate any private corruption." In the end, he was severely punished in accordance with the law. He was dismissed from his official position, the stolen grain was recovered, and the entire army was publicized to deter all those with evil intentions.
Not only did he correct corruption, Tie Xunliu also worked hard to eliminate chaos at the border. Bandits are rampant in the mountains and fields of northern Xinjiang. They have robbed people in the fields all year round, attacked grain transport teams, and destroyed grain stores in the mountains and fields. In the past, the government was unable to clean up and the defenders had no time to take care of them. The bandits became more and more rampant.
